scope.missing_positive_control_setup_deletion: sitemap.xml on a new QA baseline branch only

production_changes: Sitemap membership now requires measured HTML status 200, no error/host block/noindex and absent or exact self canonical. URL scheme, path/query case and trailing slash are preserved; host case and fragments are normalized using the existing verification URL helper.

Invalid sitemap repair re-reads and safely parses the current GitHub blob before PUT. Already parseable XML, unknown contents/SHA, unsupported encodings and unsafe entities are refused. An unknown XML encoding now returns an explicit refusal instead of an unhandled parser exception. Explicitly confirmed zero-byte blobs remain repairable, and the current blob SHA still guards concurrent writes.

The real fixture bench recrawls the repaired sitemap before preparing its robots declaration, then waits for the exact new commit. The shared build waiter can pin an expected SHA and ignores stale PR head statuses without weakening build failures or timeouts.

first_missing_attempt.diagnosis: The final-stage head identity guard could encounter the preceding successful build while GitHub propagates the PR head update. This race is reproduced by tests and prevented with an expected SHA. The first run did not retain the returned mismatching SHA or exact exception message, so it remains a failed, incomplete measurement rather than a retrospectively certified run.

explicit_counter_increase.cause: The scorer only checks reciprocity with a nonempty sitemap. Replaying the unchanged baseline HTML with the final 37 sitemap entries independently reproduces the same count and example. The original HTML already lacked this return tag.

verification.independent_countercheck: A fresh process with zero provider calls and remote writes forbidden re-read closed draft unmerged PRs, three exact build successes per case, unchanged main, two correction commits on exactly sitemap/robots, source bodies versus saved/live HTTP bodies, XML membership independently derived from observed pages, unchanged robots policy and 44 HTML routes/fields. It refused stale valid XML before PUT, retained native preview noindex, and reproduced the sole counter increase on unchanged baseline HTML with the final sitemap. After the final encoding refusal, a second fresh process repeated these checks and captured both current helper proposals before PUT: the XML is byte-identical to the measured sources.

limitations: Only two cumulative sitemap/robots cycles on the owned static HTML fixture are measured. Generated sitemaps, sitemap indexes/multiple files, unobserved URLs and arbitrary customer templates are not certified.
The built sitemap deliberately contains only eligible pages observed by this crawl, not a guarantee that every production URL has been discovered. The existing 5000-entry refusal remains.

Raw previews remain noindex. Controlled sitemap membership uses the exact saved preview XML, not the production XML that a raw crawler may follow through the absolute robots declaration. No production indexing or global raw-discovery equivalence is claimed.
One existing missing return hreflang becomes visible per case and is left unresolved. Passing the three sitemap-family targets does not mean all SEO counters are green.
The inventory catalogs exact named record references, including failed/partial records, not all successful occurrences, tests or supported stacks. It must not be used as a readiness score.

The recorded live builds/crawls precede the final unknown-encoding refusal. A fresh current-code source-only replay produces identical XML for both real baseline cases, but is not an additional post-change build or recrawl.
No agent deployment/startup/scheduler, payment acceptance, customer onboarding or capacity test is added. The 42 SQLite-run skips remain, including separately scoped PostgreSQL tests.
next_acceptance_check: Resolve the remaining evidence gaps per visible family and supported source pattern, keeping failures/refusals/partial scope distinct; then validate production lifecycle and customer onboarding before first-client readiness.
